title: ITU-T Recommendations Q.23 and Q.24: DTMF Sending and Reception
access: Full official reading access to Q.23 (11/1988) and Q.24 (11/1988), both listed by ITU-T as in force. The PDFs are freely readable but remain ITU-copyrighted; no republication or adaptation right is inferred.
topics: Q.23 §§6–7 and Fig. 1/Q.23 — low/high frequency groups, sixteen-symbol allocation, ±1.8% sending tolerance, and distortion limit.
Q.24 §§2.2–2.5 — exactly-one-per-group receiver validity, frequency tolerance, received level/twist considerations, and timing categories.
Q.24 Annex A — administration/application-specific example values, not a universal threshold profile.
key_results: The DTMF code consists of one simultaneous tone from each of two mutually exclusive four-frequency groups.
A receiver must reject cases that do not contain exactly one low-group and exactly one high-group component.
Course thresholds for twist, duration, pause, and interruption must be labeled as the selected test profile unless tied to a named Annex A administration.
pedagogy: Treat Q.23/Q.24 as a primary requirements source, not a DSP tutorial. Derive the detector from the technical texts, then use the standards to construct acceptance, rejection, and false-detection tests while preserving the distinction between in-force recommendations and locally chosen laboratory thresholds.
figures: Draw a rights-safe keypad/frequency matrix from the numeric Q.23 groups rather than reproducing the copyrighted standard figure.
Draw a receiver conformance checklist from the Q.24 parameter categories and the course's explicitly labeled test profile.
gems: Exactly one tone per group turns a frequency estimator into a structured decision rule with direct negative tests.
Q.24's administration-dependent values are a useful lesson in standards literacy: an in-force document may define the parameter set without imposing one global numerical profile.
chapter_map: Q.23 §§6–7 and Fig. 1/Q.23 → sending code and tolerances.
Q.24 Annex A → example operational values and deployment variation.
